# contagion

[![DOI](https://zenodo.org/badge/425392234.svg)](https://zenodo.org/badge/latestdoi/425392234)

**Data description**

The file entitled 'modular.Rmd' contains the source code. The secondary data can be found in the 'Data' folder. Within the folder, 'all.csv' contains all the COVID-19 incidence data publicly available in Our World in Data. The file 'state-abbrevs.csv', 'state-areas.csv' and 'state-population.csv' include the abbreviations of the states of the USA, their areas and their population respectively.

**Experimental design, materials and methods**

The program was written in R language version 4.1.2, in the Tidyverse ecosystem.

The following variables are defined in the global environment, initiated as NULL if not mentioned otherwise and populated later at the invocation of the final() function.

The 'tune\_spread' parameter determines the probability of transmitting the disease from one infected block to a susceptible block, a unit block-length away, at a fixed time from the contraction of the infection by the infector. There are several factors that affect the spread parameter like the intrinsic virulence of the virus and protective measures such as wearing masks and hand washing.

The 'total\_infective\_period' determines the total time duration an infected block can remain infectious. The model by default assumes a negative linear relationship between the time and infectivity for each infected cell. Still, the user can explicitly define a custom function for the infectivity over time.

The size of the population 'sq' is the number of total cells, which has to be a square number.

'g\_t' is the main population statistics table initially populated by the generate\_pop\_stat\_table function as described later.

'p\_list' is the list object storing the generated graphs, and 'current\_s' is the current time-step initiated as 0.

'master\_tbl' is the data frame storing all the daily population statistics with timestamps,

'c\_plt' is a data frame of daily SIR compartment counts, and 'df' is a numeric vector of the cumulative cases.

The 'mobility', 'vaccine' and 'radius' are the three variables that are incorporated into dynamic modules. These parameters are initiated as data frames containing time and value pairs. The mobilize() function calls three modules in each iteration and checks for necessary parameter adjustments.

The program is executed by calling the final() function which wraps around the helper functions and calls them in the required sequence.

```{r}
#LOESS modeling for expansion of time and population scales for R0 estimation

get_r0 <- function(sc_factor = 7, sc_pop = 100000) {
  si <- c(5.2, 4.75)
  mGT = generation.time ("gamma", si)
  days <- seq(1, by = sc_factor, length.out = length(df))
  mod <- loess(df ~ days, span = 0.2)
  day <- 1:last(days)
  cases <- predict(object = mod, newdata = day)
  d <- data.frame(day = day, cases = cases, lead = lead(cases)) %>% mutate(new = (lead - cases) * sc_pop)
  R0 <- estimate.R(round(d$new[d$new > 0]), methods = c('EG', 'ML'), GT = mGT)
  ret <- data.frame(method = c('EG', 'ML'), R0 = c(R0$estimates$EG$R, R0$estimates$ML$R), lower = c(R0$estimates$EG$conf.int[1],R0$estimates$ML$conf.int[1]), upper = c(R0$estimates$EG$conf.int[2],R0$estimates$ML$conf.int[2]))
  plt <- ret %>% ggplot(aes(x = method, col = method)) + geom_errorbar(aes(y = R0,  ymin = lower, ymax = upper)) + geom_point(aes(y = R0))
  return(list(df = ret, plt = plt))
}
```



```{r}
final <- function(s = 10, thresh = 0.2, rad = 0.2, size = 25, pop = 5, i = 1, spread = 0.2, graph_span = 0.4, vaccination_frac = 0.4, vaccine_efficacy = 0.8, sc_time = 7, sc_pop = 100000, q_inf = 0.8, q_eff = 0.0, infective_period = 10, snapshot = FALSE, fps = 10, frames = 100, filename = 'def', dark_theme = TRUE, quarentine_begin = 0, vaccination_begin = 0, sir_graph = FALSE, timeline = FALSE) {
  
  current_s <<- 0
  master_tbl <<- NULL
  tune_spread <<- spread
  total_infective_period <<- infective_period 
  quarentine_begin <<- quarentine_begin
  vaccination_begin <<- vaccination_begin 
  
  set.seed(1)
  g_t <<- generate_pop_stat_table(generate_pop_vector(size,pop), is = i)
  sq <<- size
  dff <- numeric(0L)
  dff[1] = i
  df <<- dff 
  p_list <<- NULL
  set.seed(1)
  print(plt())
  
  message('Running simulation... please wait...')
  pbreplicate(s, mobilize(g_t, thresh = thresh, rad = rad, q_inf = q_inf, q_eff = q_eff,vaccination_frac = vaccination_frac, vaccine_efficacy = vaccine_efficacy, timeline = timeline))
  
  d<- data.frame(day = 1:length(df), n = df) %>% mutate(i = n - lag(n, 1), s = pop - n)
  
  pl1 <- d %>% ggplot(aes(x = day * sc_time, y = n * sc_pop)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth(span = graph_span) + labs(x = 'Day', y = 'Total cases') + scale_y_continuous(labels = comma)
  
  pl2 <- d %>% ggplot(aes(x = day * sc_time, y = i * sc_pop / sc_time)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth(span = graph_span) + labs(x = 'Day', y = 'Cases') + scale_y_continuous(labels = comma)
  
  pc <- d %>% pivot_longer(cols = c('n', 'i', 's'), names_to = 'Compartment') %>% ggplot(aes(x = day * sc_time, y = value * sc_pop, col = Compartment)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth(span = graph_span) + theme_bw() + labs(x = 'Day', y = 'Cases') + scale_y_continuous(labels = comma)
```

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
qurantine <- function(tab, inf, efficacy) {
  #inf is the infectivity fraction at which quarantine is carried out
  days <- round(total_infective_period * inf)
  thres <- (1/total_infective_period) * days
  #ids
  inds <- which(tab$infectivity == thres)
  # print(inds)
  # print(thres)
  # print(efficacy)
  new_pos <- tab$pos
  inds <- sample(inds, (efficacy * length(inds)))
  #print(inds)
  new_pos[inds] <- 1
  tab$pos <- new_pos
  return(tab)
}
```

```{r}
calibrate <- function(s = 25, rad = 0.05, size = 90^2, pop = 4200, i = 1, vaccination_frac = 0.5, vaccine_efficacy = 0.8, sc_time = 14, sc_pop = 5000, q_inf = 0.7, q_eff = 0.6, infective_period = 4, quarentine_begin = 0, vaccination_begin = 20, grid = expand.grid(spread = seq(0.017, 0.019, by = 0.0005), thresh = seq(0.25, 0.25, by = 0.02)), graph_span = 0.2, max_target = 500000) {
  
  results <<- grid
  
  for (ii in 1:nrow(grid)) {
    current_s <<- 0
    master_tbl <<- NULL
    tune_spread <<- grid$spread[ii]
    total_infective_period <<- infective_period 
    quarentine_begin <<- quarentine_begin
    vaccination_begin <<- vaccination_begin 
    
    set.seed(1)
    g_t <<- generate_pop_stat_table(generate_pop_vector(size,pop), is = i)
    sq <<- size
    dff <- numeric(0L)
    dff[1] = i
    df <<- dff 
    p_list <<- NULL
    set.seed(1)
    print(plt())
    
    message('Running simulation... please wait...')
    pbreplicate(s, mobilize(g_t, thresh = grid$thresh[ii], rad = rad, q_inf = q_inf, q_eff = q_eff,vaccination_frac = vaccination_frac, vaccine_efficacy = vaccine_efficacy))
    
    results$error[ii] <<- sqrt((max_target - (max(df) * sc_pop))^2)
  }
  cv <- results %>% mutate(mobility = as.factor(thresh)) %>%  ggplot(aes(x = spread, y = error, col = mobility)) + geom_point() + geom_line()
  return(list(best_thresh = results$thresh[which.min(results$error)],best_spread = results$spread[which.min(results$error)], cv = cv))
}
```

```{r}
#LOESS modeling for expansion of time and population scales for R0 estimation

get_r0 <- function(sc_factor = 7, sc_pop = 100000) {
  si <- c(5.2, 4.75)
  mGT = generation.time ("gamma", si)
  days <- seq(1, by = sc_factor, length.out = length(df))
  mod <- loess(df ~ days, span = 0.2)
  day <- 1:last(days)
  cases <- predict(object = mod, newdata = day)
  d <- data.frame(day = day, cases = cases, lead = lead(cases)) %>% mutate(new = (lead - cases) * sc_pop)
  R0 <- estimate.R(round(d$new[d$new > 0]), methods = c('EG', 'ML'), GT = mGT)
  ret <- data.frame(method = c('EG', 'ML'), R0 = c(R0$estimates$EG$R, R0$estimates$ML$R), lower = c(R0$estimates$EG$conf.int[1],R0$estimates$ML$conf.int[1]), upper = c(R0$estimates$EG$conf.int[2],R0$estimates$ML$conf.int[2]))
  plt <- ret %>% ggplot(aes(x = method, col = method)) + geom_errorbar(aes(y = R0,  ymin = lower, ymax = upper)) + geom_point(aes(y = R0))
  return(list(df = ret, plt = plt))
}
```
